lobbying_summary.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–314 of 2026 (314 votes, January 6, 2026 to September 16, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

votes.plain_language: This bill lets an employee stock-ownership plan rely on an independent appraiser's value for company stock that is not publicly traded, if the appraiser follows Internal Revenue Service methods. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Faster Labor Contracts Act (H R 5408)
votes.bill_title: Faster Labor Contracts Act
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes mandatory deadlines for parties negotiating an initial collective bargaining agreement and provides for mediation and arbitration to finalize those agreements. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act (H R 2988)
votes.bill_title: Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act
votes.plain_language: This bill modifies the requirements for fiduciaries of employer-sponsored retirement plans. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act (H R 2988)
votes.bill_title: Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 2988 (Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act) modifies the requirements for fiduciaries of employer-sponsored retirement plans. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 2988)
votes.bill_title: Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 2988 (Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment requires the Government Accountability Office to publish a study on brokerage accounts.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Tipped Employee Protection Act (H R 2312)
votes.bill_title: Tipped Employee Protection Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 2312 (Tipped Employee Protection Act) modifies the definition of a tipped employee under the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to exclude consideration of an employee's duties when determining if the employee is a tipped employee. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Empowering Employer Child and Elder Care Solutions Act (H R 2270)
votes.bill_title: Empowering Employer Child and Elder Care Solutions Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 2270 (Empowering Employer Child and Elder Care Solutions Act) excludes the value of employer-funded child or dependent care from being used in calculating an eligible employee's overtime pay. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — Flexibility for Workers Education Act (H R 2262)
votes.bill_title: Flexibility for Workers Education Act
votes.plain_language: This bill modifies the definition of hours worked under the Fair Labor Standards Act to exclude certain voluntary training that occurs outside an employee's regular working hours. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.plain_language: This was a motion to adjourn the House. A Yea votes to adjourn; a Nay votes to stay in session.

votes.plain_language: This was a quorum call, which records which members are present so the House can do business. It is not a vote on any measure. Members answer present; there is no Yea or Nay.

votes.bill_title: Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community.
votes.plain_language: This resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter acts of anti-Semitism. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.
